artists.biography:
The Moody Blues are an English rock band. Among their innovations was a fusion with classical music, most notably in their 1967 album Days of Future Passed.
The Moody Blues have sold in excess of 70 million albums worldwide and have been awarded 14 platinum and gold discs. As of 2012 they remain active with one member from the original band from 1964 and two more from the 1967 lineup.

perplexity.description:
Octave is the ninth studio album by The Moody Blues, released on June 9, 1978, marking the band's return following a substantial hiatus. Produced by Tony Clarke, who would not work with the band again after this project, the album showcases the group at a creative peak, blending upbeat rock compositions with moving ballads. The record demonstrates each band member contributing their distinctive talents, resulting in a cohesive work that balances energetic rockers with introspective material across its 46-minute runtime.

The album achieved moderate commercial success, reaching number 6 on the UK charts and number 13 in the United States, where it earned Platinum certification. While Octave has not consistently ranked among the band's most celebrated releases in popular discourse, critical reassessment recognizes it as a significant entry in their catalog, with its polished production and varied songwriting earning appreciation from listeners who value the band's technical proficiency and compositional range during this period. The album was remastered and reissued in 2008 with five bonus live tracks recorded from performances in 1978 and 1979.
